description: How Starlink turned orbit into a racetrack: from a 60-satellite demo in 2019 to tens of thousands planned — and how rivals OneWeb, Amazon's Kuiper and legacy players scrambled, stalled, or quietly scaled. This dataset tracks cumulative LEO constellation satellites (per operator) year-by-year, showing one player rocketing ahead while others lag or consolidate.
youtube_description:
The Satellite Stampede — how SpaceX's Starlink turned orbital deployments into a runaway lead while rivals struggled to keep pace. This video animates cumulative LEO satellite counts (Starlink, OneWeb, Amazon's Kuiper, Telesat) from 2007–2026. Real milestones you'll see: Starlink's first 60-satellite batch in 2019, rapid scaling through 2021–2023 as SpaceX leapt into thousands of satellites, OneWeb's bankruptcy-and-rescue path and its focused ~first-gen fleet, Kuiper's slow ramp into launches, and small-scale efforts like Telesat's Lightspeed prototypes. The chart-race tells the real-world story of deployment speed, regulatory battles, and who owns low Earth orbit today. Like, comment what surprised you, and subscribe for more visual timelines. Sources: company launch manifests, regulatory filings, industry trackers and the UCS satellite database (public launch counts & press releases). #subscribe for weekly data visuals — or drop a topic you want animated next.
